title: The Stanford Encyclopedia entry "Liar Paradox" says: The first sentence in this essay is a lie.
summary: The Stanford Encyclopedia entry "Liar Paradox" says: The first sentence in this essay is a lie.
body: Beall, Jc, Glanzberg, Michael, Ripley, Ellie, Rossi, Lorenzo, in the Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy entry "Liar Paradox" says: "The first sentence in this essay is a lie. There is something odd about saying so, as has been known since ancient times. To see why, remember that all lies are untrue. Is the first sentence true? If it is, then it is a lie, and so it is not true. Conversely, suppose that it is not true. We (viz., the authors) have said it, and normally things are said with the intention of being believed. Saying something that way when it is untrue is a lie. But then, given what the sentence says, it is true after all!" This card reports that entry's preamble. It does not treat the entry as the original paper it cites.
